newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish exports rose six pct in April - exporters.
newsitem.headline: Turkish exports rose six pct in April - exporters.

text.p: Turkish exports rose by six percent to $2.0 billion in April, from $1.88 billion in the same 1996 period, the Turkish Exporter's Assembly (TIM) said on Tuesday.
Total exports had jumped 17 percent in January, 15 percent in February and 10.2 percent in March, compared with the same months last year.

"We could not maintain the speed of the upward trend seen in the first few months of this year... It will be difficult to reach the 1997 target (of around $28 billion)," TIM chairman Okan Oguz said in a statement.

Turkey's leading readywear exports rose only four percent to $528.1 million in April, from $499.4 million in the same period last year. It was followed by iron and steel exports, up 15 percent to $254.8 million and exports of textile and related raw materials, up three percent to $223.3 million.

Compared to April 1996, grain and hazelnut exports jumped 56 percent to $59.7 million, pulses and oilseed exports rose 54 percent to $153.9 million last month. Olive and olive-oil exports leapt 90 percent to $7.8 million in the same period.
TIM reported an 18 percent decline in electric-electronic exports to $138.2 million in April, compared to the same 1996 period.
It said Turkey's total exports increased 13 percent to $8.4 billion in the first four months of 1997, over the same period last year.
